concept.name: Channel
concept.definition: A chart structure formed by two parallel trendlines that enclose price action: a primary trendline along the trend's pullbacks and a parallel channel (return) line along the opposite swings. Channels frame trend direction plus likely reaction zones; they are descriptive constructs, not predictive guarantees.
concept.intuition: Price travels between two parallel rails — one rail supports it, the other caps it — until it jumps the track.
concept.mechanics: Draw the trendline through the trend's lows (uptrend) or highs (downtrend), then draw a parallel line through the opposite extreme(s). Traders reference the lower line as support and the upper as resistance; breaks of either rail are read as acceleration or potential trend change depending on direction.
concept.failure_modes: True parallel structure is rarer than textbooks suggest; forced parallelism produces channels that price ignores, and channel breaks fail like any other level break.
concept.misconceptions: That price must reverse at the channel rails; strong trends ride one rail for extended periods, and breaks of the far rail often accelerate rather than reverse the move.
concept.example: A rising stock respects a rising support line at its pullback lows while a parallel line through its rally highs caps each advance, forming an ascending channel.
